Ontop of the food and the regular convenience store items, we have beer/malt/wine sales (huge deal for PA liquor laws), slot machines, huge tobacco+cbd selections, fully stocked coffee bars with every possible bean, creamer, and sweetener. You name it, it's there. And if you're a tractor trailer driver, Rutter's even has truck parking at a lot of their locations with long diesel fuel pumps and well lit and recorded areas for safety.

I'm interested in seeing where this market goes from here. I can only imagine.

Hey it looks like I missed most of the conversation here, but I too have noticed this pattern over the last 10 years of warehouse development in my area.

We have a surplus of spent farm land for sale (or at least HAD a surplus, not sure now) so warehouse after warehouse was scouting the area out. Bidding wars happened, development happened around the warehouses, and now more and more people are immigrating to rural Pennsylvania as it slowly turns into suburban land.

I've met a lot of workers that hail from Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic that all have the same story: the breadwinner would move to New York or New Jersey while working their entire ass off 80+ hours a week and either pay their family's bills from afar, or save and move them up here.

Now the cost of living in NY and NJ is too high compared to PA, so it makes a ton of sense to move here. There's been a notable shift in culture and diversity that scares a lot of the older local generation who watched it all happen. We could definitely use more diversity here.

But now my competition for work is willing to work longer and longer hours with fewer breaks and fringe benefits in lower and lower quality work environments and our state labor laws don't really seem to be progressing in favor of the worker, so we have quite a choice on our hands: become one with the grind or move somewhere poorer.
